name: Puna
notes: Dry high-Andean puna (Peru, Bolivia, N Chile, NW Argentina) 3200-5000 m: bunchgrass steppe with Polylepis groves, resinous tola shrubs, Puya raimondii and hard cushion bogs (bofedales).

canopy.name: Queñua
canopy.source: Polylepis tarapacana, Bolivia/Chile/Peru/Argentina 4000-5200 m, world's highest tree, gnarled 2-8 m with peeling red bark

traits.native_range: Polylepis tarapacana, Bolivia/Chile/Peru/Argentina 4000-5200 m, world's highest tree, gnarled 2-8 m with peeling red bar
traits.trunk: short twisted trunk, heavy low limbs, wind-shaped
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

canopy.silhouette: stunted crooked tree with shaggy red bark

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings establish in rock crevices and between grass tussocks on volcanic slopes at 4,000-5,000 m. Young plants are tiny, stiff sprigs with small trifoliolate leaves of thick, resinous, felted leaflets crowded at the shoot tips; they grow only a few cm a year and soon show the twisted stems and flaking, many-layered, red-brown papery bark of the adult.
growth.source: Wikipedia es/en (trees 1-3.5 m, to 8 m, or shrubs 0.5-1 m; 3,900-4,700 m, to 5,200 m, the highest-growing tree; thick layered red bark). Very slow growth and ages of several centuries follow tree-ring work on this species (not re-checked here); germination and age at first flowering estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia es (flowers 0.4-0.8 cm, petal-less, 1-2 per inflorescence; flowering and fruiting Sept-Dec; one-seeded achene with glandular or woolly hairs and 3-4 spiny ridges); Wikipedia en Polylepis (wind pollinated: green sepals, no scent or nectar, fringed stigma). Timings and crop estimated.

shrub.name: Puna cactus
shrub.source: Cumulopuntia boliviana, altiplano Peru/Bolivia/Chile/Argentina 3500-4700 m, spiny mound-forming cactus 10-50 cm

traits.native_range: Cumulopuntia boliviana, altiplano Peru/Bolivia/Chile/Argentina 3500-4700 m, spiny mound-forming cactus 10-50 cm
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: low mound of spiny green segments

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: two fleshy cotyledons, then a small egg-shaped, tuberculate green segment with areoles bearing yellow to red-brown spines (plus tiny short-lived leaves at the areoles, as in all opuntioids). New segments bud from the sides one or two a year, forming short chains that slowly merge into a dense, spiny, mounded cushion up to 1 m across.
growth.source: World of Succulents (dense cushions to 1 m+, segments to 7.5 x 4 cm, spines to 10 cm, yellow flowers to 6 cm, fleshy green-yellow fruit ~2 cm); Opuntioideae seed biology (hard funicular seed coat, slow erratic germination: Opuntia tomentosa studies). Growth, age and lifespan estimated from altiplano cushion cacti.

fruiting.source: World of Succulents (flowers yellow, rarely orange/pink/red, to 5 cm long and 6 cm wide; fruit fleshy, green to yellowish, subspherical, ~2 cm, usually spineless). Flowering season (austral summer), pollinators, fruit timing and crop estimated from Opuntioideae.

shrub.name: Puna daisy shrub
shrub.source: Parastrephia lepidophylla (tola), Bolivian/Peruvian/Chilean altiplano 3500-4800 m, resinous scale-leaved shrub 0.5-1.5 m

traits.native_range: Parastrephia lepidophylla (tola), Bolivian/Peruvian/Chilean altiplano 3500-4800 m, resinous scale-leaved shrub 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings have two small cotyledons, then a sprig of minute, scale-like, overlapping resinous leaves pressed to the stem. It branches densely from the base into a rounded, dark-green, sticky, strongly aromatic shrub whose twigs look like green cords, much like a cypress or heath twig.
growth.source: Estimated from the growth form (resinous, scale-leaved shrub of the Andean puna, the dominant 'tola') and slow high-altitude shrub growth; flowering heads and achenes inferred from puna Asteraceae

fruiting.source: Estimated from Asteraceae shrubs of the puna: small yellow discoid heads solitary at the twig tips in the wet season, visited by flies and bees; tiny achenes with a white pappus shed from the opened head

shrub.name: Queen of the Andes
shrub.source: Puya raimondii, Peru/Bolivia puna 3200-4800 m, giant rosette 3 m with flowering spike to 12 m, largest bromeliad

traits.native_range: Puya raimondii, Peru/Bolivia puna 3200-4800 m, giant rosette 3 m with flowering spike to 12 m, largest bromeliad
traits.leaf_shape: stiff spined sword leaves in a rosette
traits.trunk: none or a short woody stem; tall flower spike
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: huge spiny rosette with giant flower column

growth.juvenile_note: For decades a stemless, ever-widening ball of stiff, narrow, grey-green leaves (to 1-1.25 m long) with hooked spines on the edges. Later a thick trunk up to 4 m lifts the rosette, skirted by a shaggy thatch of dead leaves. At the end a colossal spike 4-8 m tall bursts from the centre carrying thousands of flowers; after seeding the whole plant dies.
growth.source: Wikipedia Puya raimondii (flowers at 40-100 yr in the wild, 28 yr at UC Botanical Garden Berkeley; trunk to 4 m; leaves 1-1.25 m; spike 4-8 m with 8,000-20,000 flowers and ~12 million seeds; 2,400-4,200 m); germination and trunk age estimated from Puya growers

fruiting.source: Wikipedia Puya raimondii (flowers from May/Jun to mid-Dec; 3 greenish-white petals often tinged purple; 8,000-20,000 flowers per spike; capsules 2.5-3 cm; ~12 million seeds 3-5 mm; hummingbirds such as the black metaltail and perching birds such as ground doves and sierra finches take nectar); ripening and decay estimated

traits.native_range: Azorella compacta, Peru/Bolivia/Chile/Argentina 3200-5200 m, huge rock-hard bright green cushion mounds up to 1-3 m acro

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are rare: a tiny rosette of minute, stiff, glossy, leathery leaves that branches densely into a hard little bright-green dome on bare rocky ground. Shoots pack so tightly that the resinous cushion can bear a person's weight; it widens only about a centimetre a year, so a knee-high cushion is centuries old.
growth.source: Wikipedia (cushions to 6 m across at 3200-5250 m, ~1.5 cm growth per year, oldest cushions ~1.4 mm/yr, many estimated over 3000 years old; self-fertile flowers visited by flies, bees, wasps, moths); Kleier & Rundel 2004 Austral Ecol. (growth and population structure); germination and first flowering estimated.

ground.name: Bofedal cushion
ground.source: Distichia muscoides, Andean peat bogs (bofedales) 3800-5000 m, hard bright-green cushion peat former

traits.native_range: Distichia muscoides, Andean peat bogs (bofedales) 3800-5000 m, hard bright-green cushion peat former
traits.leaf_shape: tiny leaves packed in a dome
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a tiny tuft of short, stiff, two-ranked leaves a few millimetres long. Shoots branch and pack side by side into a small, hard, flat-topped, bright green cushion that spreads into sheets over the wet ground of high-Andean bogs; dead lower shoots build up underneath as peat, so the living surface rises a few cm a year.
growth.source: Wikipedia Distichia muscoides (cushion of densely packed evergreen shoots and mm-long leaves forming a firm flat surface; growth up to 5 cm/yr in favourable sites; dominates Andean bofedales over peat up to 5 m thick; year-round grazing). Germination, first flowering and cushion age estimated.

traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are tiny tufts of stiff, needle-like, grey-green leaves. They slowly thicken into a hard, spiny, hemispherical tussock of rigid pungent leaves (the Andean 'iru ichu'), which with age dies out in the middle and becomes a ring; growth is very slow in the cold, dry altiplano.
growth.source: Monteiro et al. 2011, Flora 206 (tussocks 0.3-0.6 m tall, ~0.4 m wide, 46-83% dead matter, ageing into rings with a bare centre; cited by an earlier research pass). Germination and ages estimated from Andean tussock grasses.

ground.name: Ground rosette
ground.source: Werneria nubigena, Peru/Bolivia puna 3800-4800 m, flat ground-hugging rosette with white daisy flowers

traits.native_range: Werneria nubigena, Peru/Bolivia puna 3800-4800 m, flat ground-hugging rosette with white daisy flowers
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

ground.silhouette: flat ground rosette with white daisy

growth.juvenile_note: A tiny flat rosette of narrow, thick, fleshy, grass-like leaves pressed into wet peat or bog cushion, the leaf bases sheathing. It thickens a short buried stem and rhizome and slowly widens into a tight rosette, then a small clonal patch; the large white-rayed daisy heads, often pink-flushed beneath, sit almost stemless in the centre.
growth.source: Spanish Wikipedia (Rockhausenia or Werneria nubigena, condor cebolla): high Andean bogs (bofedales) from Costa Rica to Argentina, forming very large populations that can cover whole bogs. Rosette spread, germination, flowering age and lifespan estimated from Andean rosette daisies.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are thin, wiry, grey-green tufts of rolled, needle-like leaves that establish with the summer rains of the puna. They thicken slowly into dense, stiff, straw-yellow bunches, sending up silky, feathery panicles with fine awns; old tussocks carry a skirt of dead straw and resprout after burning.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Jarava ichu: a common grass of the Andean altiplano from Mexico to Argentina, fodder); timings estimated from Andean puna tussock grasses.

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seedling with two rounded cotyledons, then a flat rosette of small, fleshy, spoon-shaped leaves pressed to the puna soil; it grows into a tight little cushion of rosettes a few cm across, studded in season with upright tubular flowers.
growth.source: Estimated from Andean Gentianella biology (small rosette or cushion herbs of puna and paramo) and Gentianaceae germination (cold-stratified, slow); no species-specific data found.
